questions.q: Why shouldn't a change's risk value just be a free-text field or dropdown the requester sets themselves?
options: Because risk needs to be calculated consistently from real answers, not left to whatever the requester feels like picking
Because requesters are not allowed to open change requests
Because free-text fields cannot exist on the change_request table
Because risk only matters for Standard changes
questions.explain: A manually chosen risk value means equally dangerous changes can land on completely different risk levels depending on who fills out the form.

questions.q: How is a Risk Assessment questionnaire commonly built in a real implementation?
options: As a hardcoded approval chain with no questions at all
As a set of variables or a dedicated record answered when the Normal change is created, asking about real conditions like production impact and backout plans
As a report that runs only after the change has already been implemented
As a single yes/no toggle with no underlying questions
questions.explain: Real questionnaire questions capture concrete, checkable facts — production impact, CI criticality, backout plan, prior success — not vague impressions.

questions.q: What are two real approaches to calculating a risk band from questionnaire answers?
options: A weighted scoring model, or a rules-based lookup where certain answer combinations force a risk band
Randomly assigning High, Medium, or Low on each submission
Asking the CAB to vote on every single change's risk level before the questionnaire is even submitted
Copying the risk level from the most recently implemented change
questions.explain: Weighted scoring (points mapped to thresholds) and rules-based lookups (specific combinations forcing a band) are both defined, repeatable calculation methods.

questions.q: Why is a calculated risk value that nobody acts on worse than having no risk field at all?
options: It creates the appearance of governance without any real downstream effect, while still looking correct in reports
It automatically blocks every change from being approved
It removes the need for a Change Advisory Board entirely
It makes Standard changes impossible to create
questions.explain: A risk label that doesn't drive more approval stages gives false confidence that risk is being managed when it actually isn't.

questions.q: What does a correctly implemented risk field look like, versus a weak implementation?
options: Correct: read-only and system-calculated from questionnaire answers. Weak: manually settable by the requester or assignee regardless of the questionnaire
Correct: always defaults to Low. Weak: always defaults to High
Correct: hidden from everyone except the CAB. Weak: visible to all users
Correct: recalculated only once a year. Weak: recalculated on every form load
questions.explain: Making the field read-only and driven only by the real questionnaire answers is what prevents someone from marking a high-risk change as Low by simply selecting it.
